message: Good morning, Rich. Week 1 starts Monday, so today is an easy one: get your tools and your linear algebra ready.
summary: Almost everything in this plan is arithmetic on vectors. A vector is just an ordered list of numbers, like [0.2, -1.3, 0.7]. A model turns each token into a vector, and its weights are mostly big grids of numbers (matrices) that transform those vectors.

The dot product multiplies two vectors position by position and adds up the results. When two vectors point in a similar direction, the dot product is large. That single idea returns three times: in attention (Week 3), when tokens decide which other tokens matter; in matrix multiplication, which is many dot products at once; and in semantic search (Week 7), where similar meanings have similar vectors.
You don't need proofs. You need to picture a vector as an arrow, know that a matrix moves arrows around, and be comfortable doing both in numpy.

keyTerms.meaning: An ordered list of numbers; picture it as an arrow from the origin.
A grid of numbers that transforms vectors. A model's weights are mostly matrices.
Multiply matching entries and sum them. Large when two vectors point the same way.
Many dot products at once: each row of one matrix against each column of the other.

task: Open a notebook, create two numpy vectors, and compute their dot product with np.dot. Then multiply a 2×3 matrix by a 3×2 matrix and check the output shape is 2×2. Confirm your LLM API key works.
